area: Cmd+P command palette — open latency, typing, file/content/branch search, and jank
timeline:
COLD FIRST Cmd+P (measured 328-357 ms — the user's "palette does not open instantly"):
1. t=0 keydown 'Meta' hits the window listener in useAppShortcuts.handleKeyDown (src/renderer/src/App.tsx:215-216) -> preloadCommandPalette() starts import('./CommandPalette') (App.tsx:93-97). ~0 ms.
2. t=+1 keydown 'p' with metaKey -> commandFromEvent -> runCommand('goToFile'|'openCommandPalette') (App.tsx:1007-1012) -> commandPalette.open() (App.tsx:138-145).
3. controllerRef.current is null because warm() only runs inside a requestIdleCallback that has not fired at ~540 ms after launch (App.tsx:977-983), so open() falls through to mountAndOpen() -> setMounted(true) (App.tsx:124-131). ~0 ms.
4. App re-renders; AppLayout renders <Suspense fallback={null}><CommandPaletteController/></Suspense> (App.tsx:575-595). The React.lazy at App.tsx:98-100 throws, the boundary commits a null fallback and stamps react-dom's globalMostRecentFallbackTime. ~2 ms.
5. The chunk actually loads in 8 ms (Network: requestWillBeSent 556 ms -> responseReceived 564 ms after launch). Evaluating it costs 23 ms.
6. ~295 ms of nothing. react-dom 19.2.8 throttles the Suspense retry until globalMostRecentFallbackTime + FALLBACK_THROTTLE_MS (300 ms) — node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js:27346, applied at :16688 and :18609. CPU profile of that window: 264 ms idle out of 382 ms.
7. t=+328 the retry commits: CommandPaletteController mounts, attach() sees openOnMountRef and calls handle.open() (App.tsx:114-119), CommandPalette mounts, useLayoutEffect calls dialog.showModal() + input.focus() (CommandPalette.tsx:177-184). The first frame after that is 34-69 ms because .command-palette gets backdrop-filter: blur(30px) saturate(180%) over a full-window scrim dialog (styles.css:2981-2985, :2137).
WARM Cmd+P (after the idle warm has run): controllerRef is non-null, so open() is just setOpen(true) in the already-mounted controller (CommandPalette.tsx:479-503) -> 9-13 ms end to end.

PER KEYSTROKE (measured 2.4 RepositoryWorkspace renders per character; p50 frame 8.4 ms on this 3026-path repo):
a. input onChange -> updateQuery (CommandPalette.tsx:346-352): setQuery + setActiveIndex(0) urgent, then startTransition(onQueryChange(query)).
b. Urgent render of CommandPalette only: rankPaletteEntries over ~7 command entries + up to 5 branches (paletteCommands.ts:46-62) and groupPaletteEntries — well under 0.1 ms. File rows still show the previous results for this frame (intentional).
c. Transition render in AppLayout: search.changeQuery (useRepositorySearch.ts:59-62) does setQuery + setContentResults([]) — a fresh [] literal, so the state identity always changes.
d. useRepositorySearch recomputes fileResults = rankFilePaths(indexedPaths, deferredQuery, 32, priorityPaths) (useRepositorySearch.ts:54-57) -> 0.25-0.46 ms at 3026 paths, 1.0-2.9 ms at 20k. createFileSearchIndex is NOT rebuilt, because samePathList retains the array identity across ticks (snapshotPaths.ts:22-29, App.tsx:876-879).
e. AppLayout recomputes workspaceContentSearch = {query, results} (App.tsx:555-558). Because contentResults is a new [] and query changed, this object is new every keystroke, so memo on AgentSessionLayout (App.tsx:364) fails -> RepositoryWorkspace (RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1285, memo) fails on the contentSearch prop -> RepositoryDiffPanel -> DiffSurface re-renders and recomputes searchMarkers (DiffSurface.tsx:367-372).
f. The content-search effect then runs (useRepositorySearch.ts:64-96): setContentResults([]) AGAIN (new array), setSearchingContent(true), an ipcRenderer.send cancelContentSearch to main (preload/index.ts:88 -> main/index.ts:733 -> repositorySessions.ts:56-59) even when nothing is running, and a 240 ms setTimeout. Those two writes produce a second AppLayout commit and a second full workspace re-render — hence 2.4 workspace renders per character.
g. CommandPalette re-renders with the new fileResults: searchFileActions rebuilds 12 PaletteAction objects with fresh closures (CommandPalette.tsx:258-272), contentActions 8 more (:274-290), results/groups rebuild (:292-311), all <=30 rows re-render. Keys are stable (file:<path>) so DOM nodes are reused.
h. 240 ms after the last keystroke the timeout fires; ipcRenderer.invoke('repository:search-content') reaches RepositoryService.searchContent (repository.ts:1691-1786): it kills any active rg, spawns ripgrep --json --fixed-strings --smart-case --max-columns 500 --max-count 20 with 52 exclusion globs, JSON.parses every emitted line on the main-process event loop until MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS=200 (repository.ts:117), then kills the child. Measured 55-130 ms on this repo; 271 ms end to end from last keystroke to the Content group appearing.
i. All 200 results are structured-cloned to the renderer; the palette renders 8 (MAX_CONTENT_RESULTS, CommandPalette.tsx:45) and DiffSurface turns the ones matching the open file into markers. contentResults changing identity again -> a third workspace render.
j. Closing the palette calls onQueryChange('') (CommandPalette.tsx:488) -> changeQuery('') -> two more workspace renders.

BACKGROUND LOAD ON THE SAME PATH: RepositoryWatcher debounces filesystem events 80 ms (350 ms metadata-only) and calls RepositoryService.refresh (repositoryWatcher.ts:243-323, :7-12). refresh() Promise.all's three git commands (repository.ts:1341-1354); the third, `ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard` with 52 exclusion pathspecs, measures 3.442 s wall / 1.943 s user / 1.492 s sys and returns 405 paths, so every tick burns ~3.4 CPU-seconds in a child process while the user types. Snapshot publishing itself is already cheap: #visiblePaths caches and returns the same array (repository.ts:1378-1400) and RepositoryWatcher#publish omits `paths` when the reference is unchanged (repositoryWatcher.ts:325-339), so the big path payload is not re-cloned per tick and the renderer's search index is not rebuilt. On this machine typing stayed smooth (p50 8.4 ms) during a tick, so the git walk is a CPU/battery and refresh-latency problem rather than a direct source of palette jank.

findings.title: First Cmd+P after launch costs ~330 ms of pure React Suspense fallback throttling, not work
findings.mechanism: commandPalette.open() finds controllerRef.current == null (warm(), which pre-mounts the controller, is scheduled on requestIdleCallback and has not fired at ~540 ms after launch), so it flips `mounted` and React first renders <Suspense fallback={null}><CommandPaletteController/></Suspense> with a React.lazy that throws. Committing that null fallback stamps react-dom's globalMostRecentFallbackTime; when the 10 KB chunk resolves 8 ms later, react-dom 19.2.8 refuses to commit the retry until globalMostRecentFallbackTime + FALLBACK_THROTTLE_MS (300 ms). The user waits ~330 ms while the renderer sits idle.
findings.evidence: In-page MutationObserver with CDP off the critical path: 328 ms from the Cmd+P keydown to dialog-in-DOM + open + input focused. Repeats: 355/348/357/334/324/328 ms. Presses 2-8 in the same session: 9/10/10/9/10/9/13 ms. Network domain: CommandPalette-Dr1EGm0G.js requestWillBeSent 556 ms, responseReceived 564 ms (8 ms). A control `await import('./assets/PerformanceChart-*.js')` fired from the page at the same instant took 13 ms (and 2-4 ms later in the session). CPU profile of the 382 ms window: 264 ms `(idle)`, 78 ms `(program)`, 23 ms evaluating the palette chunk. node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js:27346 `FALLBACK_THROTTLE_MS = 300`, applied at :16688 and :18609.
findings.fix: Stop suspending for the palette. Replace the React.lazy/Suspense pair with the module-store + useSyncExternalStore pattern the codebase already uses for the workspace (src/renderer/src/workspaceBoot.ts:13-61): add `const commandPalette = createModuleStore(() => import('./CommandPalette'))`, render `Controller == null ? null : <Controller .../>` in AppLayout with no Suspense boundary, and call `commandPalette.load()` from mountApp in src/renderer/src/boot.tsx:13-30 next to preloadWorkspaceRoot so the 10 KB chunk is resolved before first paint. Then delete the mounted/warm/requestIdleCallback machinery (App.tsx:102-158, 977-983): with the module preloaded, mount the controller unconditionally and let its own `open` state gate the dialog. Do NOT simply move warm() earlier — it pays the same 300 ms throttle, just invisibly, and still loses the race when the user presses Cmd+P in the first half second.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~320 ms on the first Cmd+P of every launch (330 ms -> ~10 ms)

findings.title: Empty query lists 7 commands and 1 file; repository files are never offered as autocomplete and folders never appear at all
findings.mechanism: With an empty query the palette ranks only [...commandActions, ...recentFileActions]. useRepositorySearch returns [] for fileResults whenever `searching` is false (deferredQuery.trim() === ''), so no repository file is offered until the user types. recentFiles is additionally wiped to [] on every snapshotRoot change (App.tsx:984-986), so after a restore the list holds exactly the one restored selectedPath. Separately the search index is built from snapshot.paths, which is `git ls-files` output — files only — so a directory can never be a result even when typed in full.
findings.evidence: Measured on a cold restore of materialsx-core-3: {rows: 8, groups: ['Commands','Files'], titles: ['Open repository','Toggle explorer','Toggle word wrap','Toggle context folding','Toggle terminal','Open folder','Open settings','.DS_Store']}. createFileSearchIndex (fileSearch.ts:84-91) maps paths 1:1 with no directory synthesis; RepositoryWorkspace already derives directories via getDirectoryPaths (RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1180) but never passes them to the palette.
findings.fix: (a) In useRepositorySearch.ts:54-57 drop the `!searching` early return and return the first N paths in a cheap priority order when the query is empty — rankFilePaths already returns score 0 for an empty query (fileSearch.ts:14), so `rankFilePaths(indexedPaths, '', 32, priorityPaths)` gives priority-first (changed/review files) ordering for free at 0.25 ms. (b) In CommandPalette.tsx:297-303 render Files above Commands for the empty query. (c) Feed directories into the index: extend createFileSearchIndex to take a second `directories` list built once in useRepositorySearch with the same collectDirectoryPaths helper the workspace uses, and tag IndexedPath with kind 'file'|'directory' so folder rows use IconFolder and reveal in the explorer. (d) Persist recentFiles per root instead of discarding them at App.tsx:984-986 so a restore starts with a real MRU list.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 0 ms of CPU, but removes the perceived 'palette knows nothing until I type', which is the top user complaint on this surface

findings.title: Each palette keystroke re-renders the whole workspace tree ~2.4 times because contentResults is reset to a fresh [] twice per keystroke
findings.line: 59-62 (changeQuery setContentResults([])), 77-78 (effect setContentResults([]) + setSearchingContent(true)); App.tsx:555-558 (workspaceContentSearch useMemo); App.tsx:364 (AgentSessionLayout memo); RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1285
findings.mechanism: changeQuery writes setContentResults([]) with a fresh array literal, and the effect at :64-96 writes another fresh [] plus setSearchingContent(true) in the same keystroke. Both change state identity so React commits twice. AppLayout's workspaceContentSearch useMemo depends on search.contentResults and search.query, so it yields a new object on each commit; that object defeats memo on AgentSessionLayout, which cascades to RepositoryWorkspace (memo, contentSearch prop) -> RepositoryDiffPanel -> DiffSurface, whose searchMarkers useMemo is keyed on the contentSearch object identity (DiffSurface.tsx:367-372). This only bites in workspaceView === 'file'; in review ('multi') view workspaceContentSearch is undefined and stable so memo holds.
findings.evidence: Read the live counter that RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1298 feeds (reviewMetrics.ts:21-23) through the PerformanceHud diagnostics panel: 'Workspace renders' was 4 before the palette opened, 4 after opening it, and 23 after typing 8 characters — 19 extra renders, 2.375 per keystroke, and 0 for the open itself.
findings.fix: Three independent changes, any of which cuts the cascade: (1) keep a module-level frozen EMPTY_CONTENT_RESULTS array and set that instead of a new [] at useRepositorySearch.ts:61 and :77 so React bails out when results are already empty; (2) collapse the two writes — move setContentResults(EMPTY)/setSearchingContent(true) out of the effect and do it once inside changeQuery, leaving the effect to only schedule/cancel; (3) stop threading the live query through the workspace — publish {query, results} as one state object written only when a search settles, so its identity changes at most once per search instead of three times per keystroke.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~2 workspace re-renders per keystroke removed; ~0.5 ms/keystroke on this 3026-path repo, materially more with a large file open in CodeMirror or a big review mounted

findings.title: Every refresh on the palette's data path costs 3.44 s of git walking to find 405 paths
findings.mechanism: The third parallel command, `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard -z -- . <52 exclude pathspecs>`, makes git walk the entire working tree including node_modules, .venv and every build directory; the pathspecs only filter the output. It gates the whole Promise.all, so open, session restore and every watcher tick (repositoryWatcher.ts:305) take at least 3.4 s and burn ~3.4 CPU-seconds in a child process. That competes with ripgrep and with the renderer for cores throughout the palette's life, and it is why the first-Cmd+P window sits on a busy machine.
findings.evidence: Reproduced the lead's timing on ~/Developer/materialx/materialsx-core-3: real 3.442 s, user 1.943 s, sys 1.492 s, 405 paths returned. The sibling commands in the same Promise.all: `ls-files --cached -z` 19 ms, `status --porcelain=v2 --branch -z --untracked-files=all` 48 ms.
findings.fix: Do not ask git to walk ignored files on the refresh path. Either (a) drop the third command from refresh() and populate the ignored-but-visible set lazily in the background after the snapshot is published (those paths only exist so gitignored-but-interesting files appear in the tree and in Cmd+P), or (b) replace it with the ripgrep call the folder path already uses — `rg --files --no-require-git --hidden --no-ignore-vcs` with RIPGREP_EXCLUSION_ARGS (repository.ts:304-322) prunes excluded directories during the walk instead of after it, and repository.ts:1402-1418 is the working template. Either way keep the existing #visiblePaths buffer cache (repository.ts:1378-1400) so unchanged ticks stay free.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~3.4 s off every open/restore/watcher refresh; removes ~3.4 CPU-seconds of contention per tick

findings.title: The palette's query state lives in AppLayout, so every character re-renders the application shell
findings.mechanism: useRepositorySearch owns query, contentResults and searchingContent and is called at the top of AppLayout — the component that also renders AgentSessionLayout (the entire chrome plus workspace) and TerminalDock. A keystroke in a transient overlay therefore re-renders the root of the application tree. React Compiler memoization keeps today's cost low, but it is the structural reason CP-3 can cascade at all: nothing between the input and the workspace can stop the update.
findings.evidence: App.tsx:554 `const search = useRepositorySearch(workspace.snapshot, workspace.setError, workspace.gitWorkflow.repositoryReview)` sits inside `const AppLayout = memo(function AppLayout(view: AppLayoutProps)` (App.tsx:543), whose JSX at :596-600 renders `<AgentSessionLayout key={agentSessionKey} {...workspace} workspaceContentSearch={workspaceContentSearch} />`. Measured consequence: 19 RepositoryWorkspace renders for 8 keystrokes (CP-3).
findings.fix: Move useRepositorySearch inside CommandPaletteController (or a small provider mounted next to it) so query/file-result state never reaches AppLayout. The only consumer outside the palette is DiffSurface's search markers; publish those through a tiny external store (useSyncExternalStore) or a dedicated context that DiffSurface subscribes to directly, updated only when a search settles. AppLayout then re-renders zero times per keystroke instead of two.
findings.estimatedGainMs: Removes 2 app-shell renders per keystroke and is the structural guard that stops CP-3 regressing

findings.title: Content search ships 200 ripgrep hits over IPC to render 8, and re-spawns ripgrep from scratch for every settled query
findings.mechanism: Each settled query spawns a fresh ripgrep, and the main process JSON.parses every emitted line on its event loop until 200 results accumulate, then kills the child. All 200 ContentSearchResult objects (path, line, column, up to a 500-column preview) are structured-cloned to the renderer; the palette displays 8 and DiffSurface turns the handful matching the open file into markers. Process spawn plus the fixed 240 ms debounce put a hard ~300 ms floor on the first content result even though ripgrep itself costs 55 ms here.
findings.evidence: Measured end to end: 181 ms after the last keystroke plus the 90 ms inter-key gap = 271 ms until the Content group appeared. ripgrep with the app's exact argv on materialsx-core-3: 'mat' 129 ms (17,254 JSON lines), 'material' 55 ms, 'import' 54 ms, no-match 'zzqqxx' 54 ms. repository.ts:1723 `if (results.length >= MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS || line.length === 0) return` and :1754 `if (results.length >= MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS) child.kill()`.
findings.fix: (a) Cut MAX_SEARCH_RESULTS to what the two consumers need — 24 for the palette list — and pass the currently open path in the request so main can return {top: 24, forOpenPath: [...]} and keep the marker set complete without shipping 200 rows. (b) Make the debounce adaptive: contentSearchDelay (contentSearchScheduler.ts:4-9) already returns 0 for a paste-sized jump; add a rule returning ~90 ms once the query is >= 5 characters. (c) Add `--max-filesize 1M` and cap `--threads` below the core count in the argv at repository.ts:1698-1713 so a content search cannot starve the renderer on a large repository. (d) Larger optional win: keep one long-lived rg per repository instead of spawning per query.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~150 ms off the first content result, and a ~15x smaller IPC payload per query

findings.title: The palette's first frame costs 34-69 ms because backdrop-filter: blur(30px) allocates a full-window render surface on show
findings.line: 2981-2985 (.command-palette backdrop-filter), 2137 (.command-palette-layer full-viewport dialog with var(--scrim)), 2138-2139 (::backdrop opacity transition + @starting-style)
findings.mechanism: dialog.showModal() promotes the layer to the top layer and the compositor must allocate a backdrop render surface and snapshot everything beneath it to run blur(30px) saturate(180%) for the 620x560 panel. The panel already sits on a 54%-black scrim so most of the blur is invisible, but the cost lands on exactly the frame the user is watching for.
findings.evidence: rAF frame log across the cold open: [69.3, 0.2, 32.1, 2.3, 4.2] ms; worst frame in the in-page cold-open window 33.8 ms. On the 120 Hz display observed here that is 4-8 dropped frames. Warm opens (presses 2-8) complete in 9-13 ms with normal frames, i.e. the surface is reused once it exists.
findings.fix: Reduce blur(30px) to blur(12-16px) — indistinguishable over a 54% scrim — or drop backdrop-filter on .command-palette entirely and use the opaque --popover background the reduced-transparency branch at styles.css:2989 already defines. If the glass is wanted, keep the dialog in the DOM permanently (CP-1's fix does this anyway) and add `will-change: backdrop-filter` to .command-palette so the surface is allocated before the first show.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~30-60 ms off the frame the palette appears on

findings.title: Every keystroke fires a cancelContentSearch IPC to main even when no search is running
findings.mechanism: The effect runs on every query change and unconditionally calls window.repository.cancelContentSearch() — once on the short-query branch and once on the search branch — before any search has been scheduled. Each call is an ipcRenderer.send (preload/index.ts:88) handled at main/index.ts:733 -> repositorySessions.cancelActiveContentSearch() (repositorySessions.ts:56-59) -> RepositoryService.#cancelActiveSearch() (repository.ts:2695-2702), a no-op when #activeSearch is null but still a main-process wake-up plus a bumped cancelled metric.
findings.evidence: useRepositorySearch.ts:71 `if (hasSnapshot) window.repository?.cancelContentSearch()` inside the `< CONTENT_SEARCH_MIN_QUERY_LENGTH` branch, and :79 `window.repository?.cancelContentSearch()` before the timeout is scheduled; searchContent already calls this.#cancelActiveSearch() itself at repository.ts:1693.
findings.fix: Track whether a request is actually outstanding (a ref set when the timeout fires, cleared in .finally) and send the cancel only when it is true. Main already cancels the previous search when a new searchContent arrives, so the renderer-side cancel is only needed for a search the user has abandoned.
findings.estimatedGainMs: ~8 needless main-process IPC wake-ups per typed word

findings.title: Row pointer-enter handlers re-render the whole result list, and rowRefs is never trimmed
findings.mechanism: onPointerEnter={() => setActiveIndex(index)} is attached to every row. While typing, result rows shift under a stationary cursor, so each commit fires pointerenter on whatever row lands under the pointer and schedules another CommandPalette render of all <=30 rows. rowRefs.current is an array indexed by row position, written on every render and never truncated, so it retains stale nodes from longer result sets.
findings.evidence: CommandPalette.tsx:428-438 attaches both `ref={(node) => { rowRefs.current[index] = node }}` and `onPointerEnter={() => setActiveIndex(index)}` per row. The scrollIntoView effect at :315-319 is correctly guarded by scrollActiveRowRef, so it is not a per-keystroke layout read, and keys are stable (`file:<path>`, `content:<path>:<line>:<col>:<i>`) so DOM nodes are reused.
findings.fix: Move selection to one delegated pointermove/pointerover handler on .command-palette-results that reads data-index off event.target.closest('button'), and ignore pointer events until the pointer actually moves (track lastPointerClientX/Y and bail when unchanged) so a re-render under a stationary cursor cannot change the selection. Reset rowRefs.current.length = results.length at the top of the render.
findings.estimatedGainMs: Removes up to one extra 30-row palette render per keystroke when the cursor rests over the list

findings.title: Fuzzy ranking runs on the renderer main thread and is the part that scales badly with repository size
findings.mechanism: rankFilePaths does a full linear scan with a bounded max-heap over every IndexedPath for every keystroke, inside a useDeferredValue render on the main thread. It is comfortably fast at the current repository size but it is O(paths) per character with no prefix/trigram narrowing, so it is what turns into jank on a 50-100k-path monorepo, competing with the same thread that has to paint the dropdown.
findings.evidence: Bun benchmark against the real 3026-path list from ~/Library/Application Support/Horus/last-workspace.json: 1-char 0.249 ms, 3-char 0.275 ms, 8-char 0.324 ms, worst-case subsequence 0.461 ms. Synthetic 20,000 paths: 1.519 / 1.679 / 2.107 / 2.942 ms. createFileSearchIndex: 0.468 ms at 3k, 2.983 ms at 20k. Live frames while typing 'material' on the real repo: p50 8.4 ms, p95 10.2 ms, max 19.3 ms, zero longtask entries — not a problem today.
findings.fix: Do not rewrite this now; it is not the current bottleneck. When the app needs 50k+ paths, add incremental narrowing (keep the previous query's surviving candidates and re-rank only those when the new query strictly extends the old one, turning most keystrokes into O(previous results)), and only then consider moving createFileSearchIndex + rankFilePaths into a worker. Keep the index build where it is: samePathList (snapshotPaths.ts:22-29) already retains the paths array identity across watcher ticks, so the 0.5-3 ms index build does not run per tick.
findings.estimatedGainMs: 0 ms today; prevents 3-15 ms per keystroke on large monorepos

findings.title: Per-render allocations in the palette body: unmemoized PR-selector parsing and full re-tokenizing of every content preview
findings.line: 173-175 (parsePullRequestSelector/paletteFilterQuery on every render), 132-146 (SearchPreview), 258-290 (searchFileActions/contentActions rebuild 20 action objects per keystroke)
findings.mechanism: parsePullRequestSelector runs two regexes per render outside any memo; SearchPreview is memo'd but receives `query`, which changes every keystroke, so all 8 content previews are re-tokenized with a global regex matchAll and re-split for highlighting (searchPreview.ts:50-63); searchFileActions and contentActions allocate 20 fresh objects with fresh closures per keystroke. Individually tiny, collectively the palette's per-keystroke garbage.
findings.evidence: CommandPalette.tsx:173 `const selector = parsePullRequestSelector(query)` at component scope; :276 `.map((result, index) => ({ ... run: () => { ... } }))`; searchPreview.ts:56 `for (const match of preview.matchAll(pattern))` then :63 `tokens.flatMap((token) => splitQueryMatches(token, normalizedQuery))`. The typing CPU profile shows 163 ms of JS across a 2269 ms window with no single hot frame, consistent with diffuse allocation rather than one hot loop.
findings.fix: Wrap selector/filterQuery/commandOnly in one useMemo on `query`. Give SearchPreview a stable `query` by passing the settled search query rather than the live keystroke query (this falls out of CP-3's fix). Hoist the row `run` callbacks: give each button data-action-id and use one delegated onClick on .command-palette-results that looks the action up in a Map, so the action objects become plain data memoizable per path instead of per keystroke.
findings.estimatedGainMs: sub-millisecond per keystroke; mainly reduces GC pressure during fast typing

openQuestions: Reproduce the palette measurements on a repository an order of magnitude larger than materialsx-core-3 (2,621 tracked / 3,026 snapshot paths). Everything measured here — 0.25 ms ranking, p50 8.4 ms frames, zero longtasks — says the typing path is currently healthy at this size, so the user's 'janky while typing' likely comes from a bigger workspace or from CP-7's 3.4 s refresh competing for CPU. Note the lead's 20,000-path / 1.9 MB last-workspace.json no longer matches disk: the current file is 198,124 bytes with 3,026 paths.

During the first benchmark run the Electron browser process stopped answering CDP for >60 s (both Runtime.evaluate and Input.dispatchKeyEvent timed out) roughly 4-5 s after the shell became usable. It did not reproduce across six later runs, and at least one occurrence is explained by a sibling agent in this workflow quitting the same app. Worth one dedicated run with `sample` attached to the main process, because a multi-second main-process stall would freeze every surface, not just the palette.

Confirm that review ('multi') view really is immune to CP-3. The code path says yes (workspaceContentSearch is undefined at App.tsx:556 and therefore stable), but the workspace-render counter was only read in file view; repeating that measurement with a PR review open would settle it.

RepositoryWorkspace.tsx:1223-1255 passes renderRowDecoration and contextMenu.render closures to useFileTree, which only reads its options in a useState initializer (node_modules/@pierre/trees/dist/react/useFileTree.js:6). Those closures capture the first render's snapshot.root and pathSet forever. Not a perf issue, but it is a live correctness bug in the same file and should be routed to whoever owns the explorer.
The warm() path (App.tsx:132-137, 977-983) becomes dead code once CP-1 is fixed; confirm nothing else depends on commandPaletteMounted before deleting it.

All app-level timings were taken on ~/Applications/Horus.app built 2026-09-04 12:32, which matches the current working tree's renderer sources (mtimes 12:29-12:32). Any implementer should rebuild and re-baseline before and after each fix.
